summary: Walks img->fadeTable(+0x24): {u16 count; FadeChannel *array(+4)} and calls clut_fade_apply (F_0100B6D0) on each 0x20-byte channel. NOTE: two unreferenced functions (0x0100B808, 0x0100BB28) are merged into this block — see boundary_fixes.

name: F_0100B808

name: F_0100BB28

name: clut_fade_finish_all
summary: For every fade channel: reset (F_0100B680), force dirty (+0x1F = 1), then apply (F_0100B6D0) — snaps all palette fades to their initial/committed state.

name: clut_fade_table_relocate
summary: Rebases the fade table after a load-address move: +4 channel-array pointer += delta; per channel rebases +8 (dest CLUT) and +0xC (keyframe/palette rows; also each 8-byte row's +4 pointer), then resets the channel via F_0100B680. Called only from tex1_relocate.

name: tex1_upload_to_vram
summary: Uploads all texture pieces over GIF (DMA ch2, PATH3): first gfx_sync_pipeline (F_0100D7B0); then for each 0xC transfer record {void *data,+4 u16 vramBase,+8 u16 w,+0xA u16 h} builds a 6-qword BITBLTBUF/TRXPOS/TRXREG/TRXDIR+IMAGE header on the stack via F_0100E0A0 (returns data qwc), FlushCache(0)=F_0101BE60, locks GIF sema (F_0100CC78(2)), sends header then data via gfx_dma_send (F_0100CE68 ch2), unlocks (F_0100CC98(2)); finally gfx_dma_sync(2) (F_0100CCB8).

name: gfx_set_texture_regs
summary: Applies a texture register block {TEX0 (+0), TEX1 (+8), MIPTBP1 (+0x10), MIPTBP2 (+0x18), CLAMP/TEXA (+0x20)} to the scratchpad GS context (0x70003000) shadow regs +0xD0/+0xC8/+0xB8 (+0xD8/+0xE0 when TEX1.MXL needs mips), with per-bit write-masks from the global override block at 0x1034640 (enable byte +0x1C). Recomputes TEX1.K (bits 32-43) by adding ctx+0x1C LOD bias shifted by TEX1.L (bits 19-20); handles TEX0 CLD/CSA CLUT reload bits; ORs dirty flags 0x06800680/0x01000100/0x08000800/0x10001000 into ctx+0xE8. Caller F_01000B40.

name: gfx_wait_vsync_poll
summary: Writes 8 to GS CSR (0x12001000) to clear VSINT (bit 3), busy-polls CSR&8 with a 0x3A980 timeout, then writes 8 again to re-arm. Pure-polling vertical-blank wait used before sceGsResetGraph. Callers: main (F_01000538) and gfx_init (F_0100C490).

name: gfx_reset_paths
summary: Resets the whole render pipeline: writes 1 to VIF0_FBRST (0x10003810) and VIF1_FBRST (0x10003C10), resets both VUs through cfc2/ctc2 on VU FBRST, writes 1 to GIF_CTRL (0x10003000), 4 to GIF_MODE (0x10003010), and 6 to VIF0_ERR/VIF1_ERR (0x10003820/0x10003C20). Equivalent of sceGsResetPath, hand-written by Polyphony.

name: gfx_init_vu0_constants
summary: After F_0100E404 (VU0 idle wait), loads VU0 integer regs via ctc2 (values 0x10/0x50/0x60/4/8/0xC) and stores default vectors into VU0 memory with vsqi-style cop2 ops; then writes default color/limit floats into ctx (+0x1D8=1.0, +0xBAC group from .sdata 0x1041E28, +0xB9C=255.0, +0xBB0/0xBB4=0.5) and sets gp-rel material pointer 0x1041E2C = 0x10384D8.

name: gfx_init_lights
summary: memset(ctx+0x2E0, 0, 0x680) (8 light records x 0xD0) via F_0101B1B8 (memset); sets default light colors/direction: 1.0f at +0x2FC..+0x32C/+0x348, dir z -1.0f (+0x378), 180.0f (+0x39C); calls F_0100E198; stores 0.1f (gp .lit4 0x1041D00 = 3E4CCCCD... 0.2f) into +0xA30/34/38; light count/mode bytes +0x20=7, +0x21=2.

name: gfx_init_material
summary: memset(ctx+0x960, 0, 0xA0); sets ambient 0.2f (lit4 0x1041D04) and diffuse 0.8f (0x1041D08) triples at +0x960/+0x970, alphas 1.0f; calls F_0100E198(0.0f); sets +0x9AC=1, +0xB68=2, +0xB6C=1, byte +0x22=0. Default material/shading parameters.

name: gfx_reset_blend_state
summary: Writes GS register shadow defaults into the scratchpad context: bytes +0x68=0/+0x6C=0x80, qword +0x68 &= 0xFFFF7FFF (TEST-like), +0xE8 |= 0x00801E80_00801E80 dirty bits, +0xD0=1<<34, +0xC8=0x60 (TEX1 default), +0xC0=0x0000002000000130 (ALPHA default), +0xD8/+0xE0/+0xB8=0.

name: gfx_context_init
summary: Master init of the 0xBC0-byte GS context (normally at scratchpad 0x70003000): memset(ctx,0,0xBC0); sets prim/state defaults (+0x30|=1, +0x58|=1, +0x98 &= ~0x100000001, +0xE8=0x03FF1FFF03FF1FFF, +4=8, +8=0x33E, colors +0xB60=0xFFFFFFFF, +0xB64=0x80808080, +0x1C4=2, byte +0x25=1, +0xB48/+0x15C=1.0f); then calls gfx_reset_blend_state, gfx_init_vu0_constants, gfx_init_lights and tail-calls gfx_init_material.

name: gfx_init_default
summary: Convenience wrapper: tail-jumps into gfx_init (F_0100C490) with (reset=1, inter=1, omode=arg, ffmd=1). Called from main (F_01000538).

name: gfx_init
summary: One-shot graphics system init guarded by flag 0x1041E24: memset driver globals 0x1048180 (0xC0); store mode (F_0100C848); if fullReset: gfx_wait_vsync_poll + sceGsResetGraph(0,inter,omode,ffmd) (F_010269F8), else write FLUSH (0x100) to GS CSR; save GS revision (CSR>>16) at 0x1048218; set GS IMR (0x12001010) = ~0x200 (FINISH unmasked); clear FINISH (CSR=2); set screen 0x280x0x1C0 (F_0100C9B8/F_0100C998); gfx_reset_paths; DMA init (F_0100CB08); F_0100E4E8 on VU1 microcode; install INTC handlers on causes 2 (VBlank-on, F_0100E630), 5 (VIF1, 0x100E770), 0 (GS) via AddIntcHandler (F_0101B8C0) + EnableIntc (F_0101C338); gfx_context_init on SPR 0x70003000; upload VU0 microcode (0x398B @0x1040C00 .rdata) and VU1 microcode (0x3DA8B @0x1034730 .data) via F_0100CFE8; program COP0 perf counter PCCR=0x8003783E.
sig: void gfx_init(int fullReset, short inter, short omode, short ffmd)

name: gfx_context_init_spr
summary: Wrapper: gfx_context_init(0x70003000) — reinitializes the scratchpad GS context.

name: gfx_init_vu0_constants_spr
summary: Wrapper: gfx_init_vu0_constants(0x70003000).

name: gfx_init_lights_material_spr
summary: Wrapper: gfx_init_lights(0x70003000) then gfx_init_material(0x70003000).

name: gfx_reset_blend_state_spr
summary: Wrapper: gfx_reset_blend_state(0x70003000).

name: gfx_shutdown

Called by main before launching core.gt3.

name: gfx_change_display_mode
summary: Compares args against stored mode bytes 0x1048219/1A/1B; if unchanged returns; else stores (F_0100C848), recomputes DISPLAY/PMODE shadows (F_0100C8B0) and tail-jumps to the hidden function at 0x0100C890 which calls sceGsResetGraph(5, inter, omode, ffmd). Caller F_01000C88.

name: gfx_store_display_mode

sig: void gfx_store_display_mode(int inter, int omode, int ffmd)

name: F_0100C890
summary: SPLIT-OFF (boundary fix): missed start inside F_0100C848's range: a real function tail-called by F_0100C7E0 via `j 0x100c890`

name: gfx_update_display_regs
summary: Recomputes the DISPLAY2 shadow (0x10481F0) from screen w/h (+0x94/+0x96), display area (+0x88..+0x92) and mode bytes (+0x99..+0x9B): MAGH = 0x9FF/w-1 style divide, DY base 0x19/0x24 (doubled when interlaced), DH 0x1C0/0x200 by pal/ntsc byte. Also sets PMODE shadow (+0x58) = 0x66 and BGCOLOR shadow (+0x78) = 0.

name: gfx_set_display_area
summary: Stores dx/dy/w/h at globals +0x8A/+0x88/+0x90/+0x92 then tail-calls gfx_update_display_regs. Callers: gfx_init and F_01000C88.
sig: void gfx_set_display_area(short dx, short dy, short w, short h)

name: gfx_set_screen_size
summary: Stores w/h at globals +0x94/+0x96 and tail-calls gfx_update_display_regs.

name: gfx_set_display_fb
summary: Builds DISPFB2: FBP = addr>>11, PSM = psm&0xF at bit 15, FBW = (fbw>>6)&0x3F at bit 9, DBX/DBY from stored display area; then writes GS privileged regs directly: PMODE (0x12000000) from shadow +0x58, SMODE2 (0x12000020) from +0x60, DISPFB2 (0x12000090), DISPLAY2 (0x120000A0) from +0x70, BGCOLOR (0x120000E0) from +0x78; sync.l. Polyphony's sceGsPutDispEnv equivalent (frame flip). Caller F_01000C88.
sig: void gfx_set_display_fb(u32 fbByteAddr, int psm, int fbw)

name: gfx_dma_channel_init
summary: Per-channel init using the register-base table at 0x10394D8 (ch0=VIF0 0x10008000, ch1=VIF1 0x10009000, ch2=GIF 0x1000A000): writes chcrFlags (0x40=TTE, 0xC0=TTE|TIE, 0x80=TIE) to Dn_CHCR and zeroes MADR/TADR/ASR0/ASR1/SADR; clears busy bytes at 0x1048180+ch*0xC+0x1C/0x1D; CreateSema (F_0101BBE0, init=1,max=1 mutex) -> id at 0x10481A4+ch*0xC.

name: gfx_dma_init
summary: Initializes channels 0/1/2 via F_0100CA78 (0x40/0xC0/0x80); clears D_STAT (0x1000E010) ch0-2 bits (0x70007), masks D_PCR (0x1000E020) &= 0x7FF8FFF8, D_CTRL (0x1000E000) |= 1 (DMA enable); AddDmacHandler (F_0101B8F0) for ch0/1/2 -> completion handler F_0100E8E8, ids at 0x10481A4+? (0xA4/A8/AC... stored at 0x1048224/28/2C); EnableDmac (F_0101C408) x3.

name: gfx_dma_shutdown
summary: DisableDmac (F_0101C3A0) ch0/1/2; RemoveDmacHandler (F_0101B910) with saved ids; DeleteSema (F_0101BBF0) on the three channel mutexes (0x10481A4/B0/BC).

name: gfx_dma_lock
summary: Tail-calls WaitSema (F_0101BC20) on the channel mutex at 0x1048180+ch*0xC+0x24.

name: gfx_dma_unlock
summary: Tail-calls SignalSema (F_0101BC00) on the channel mutex at 0x1048180+ch*0xC+0x24.

name: gfx_dma_sync
summary: Waits for channel completion: if busy byte (0x1048180+ch*0xC+0x1D) set, links a stack node {next, tid=GetThreadId (F_0101BAD0)} into the channel waiter list (+0x20+ch*0xC) under DI/EI (F_01022B68/F_01022BB0), SleepThread-loops (F_0101BB00) up to 0x78 times; on timeout force-clears CHCR.STR (bit 0x100) of the channel base from table 0x10394D8 and returns -1; unlinks node, CancelWakeupThread(tid) (F_0101BB30). The DMAC handler F_0100E8E8 wakes the waiters.

name: gfx_dma_send
summary: Normal-mode DMA kick: gfx_dma_sync(ch); set channel busy byte; QWC = qwc; MADR = addr (0x70000000 scratchpad addresses get the 0x80000000 SPR bit); CHCR = (CHCR & 0xFFFFFEF0) | 0x101 (DIR=to-peripheral, STR=1); sync.l.
sig: int gfx_dma_send(int ch, void *madr, u32 qwc)

name: gfx_kick_frame_lists
summary: Kicks a finished frame packet: default header from SPR ctx +0x130; lock ch1+ch2 mutexes, gfx_dma_sync(1)/(2), clear path-busy bytes 0x1048195..98, chain-kick hdr[0] on VIF1 and hdr[1] on GIF via F_0100EC20, unlock both.

name: vu_upload_microcode
summary: Builds a source-chain on the stack of DMA ref tags (id=3, 0x30000000) each carrying a VIF MPG vifcode (0x4A000000 | num<<16 | loadAddr) for up to 0x100 dwords per chunk, terminated by an end tag (0x70000000); FlushCache(0); lock channel, kick via F_0100EC20, sync, unlock. Used by gfx_init to load the VU0 (0x398B @0x1040C00) and VU1 (0x3DA8B @0x1034730) microprograms.
sig: void vu_upload_microcode(int vif /*0=VIF0,1=VIF1*/, u32 vuDestAddr, u32 byteSize, const void *code)

name: gfx_state_command
summary: Render-state dispatcher through the 109-entry jump table at 0x103E360 (.rodata). Cases clear/set bits in the SPR context: cmd0 waits for a pending chain then appends MSKPATH3(on) via F_0100D330 and sets ctx+0x1C0; others clear bits 0x40/0x20/0x80/0x10 of ctx+4, modify shadow regs +0x30/+0x40/+0x58/+0x98/+0xB0 with dirty bits into +0xE8, clear feature bytes +0x20..+0x2A, or (cmds >= 0x65) clear the enable byte of light record (cmd-0x65)*0xD0 at +0x2E8 and refresh via F_0100ECD0. Caller F_01000B40 (its 'disable/set attribute' API).

name: gfx_mskpath3
summary: Selects list 0 (F_0100D6E0(0)), calls F_0100E570, then appends one qword to the current chain (ctx+0x118): DMA cnt tag qwc=0 (0x10000000) with vifcodes FLUSH (0x11000000) and MSKPATH3 (0x06000000 | mask<<15). PATH3 masking around texture transfers.

name: gfx_set_packet_buffer
summary: Sets the display-list buffer: ctx+0x110 base, +0x114 size, +0x118 current = physical(buf) | ctx+0x124 mapping bits, +0x11C end; if ctx+0x120 set: sync.l + FlushCache(0). NOTE: two dead getters at 0x0100D410/0x0100D420 live inside this block (see boundary_fixes).

name: F_0100D420

name: gfx_begin_packet
summary: Opens a frame packet if flag ctx+0x1BE clear: reserves a 2-word header {vif1Chain, gifChain} at ctx+0x130, emits an initial DMA cnt tag (0x10000001) + GIF A+D tag writing default state (values 0x020001B3, 0x1000404, 0x300, 0x500, 0x2000, 0xC0C0C0C0), resets masks +0xE8/+0xF8=0x03FF1FFF..., clears +0xB7C/+0x128/+3/+2/+0x23/+0x1BD/+0xB74/+0xB78, sets +0x1BE=1. Returns the header pointer.

name: gfx_end_packet
summary: Closes the open frame packet: if split flag +0x1BF, first F_0100D5E0; then writes DMA end tags (0x70000000) into both the primary (+0x118 or +0x128) and secondary (+0x12C) chain tails, clears +0x1BE, and if +0x120==0: sync.l + FlushCache(0).

name: gfx_close_subpacket
summary: If flag +0x1BF: restores register mask +0xE8 from +0xF0 (also patched into the qword at +0x134->+8), terminates the current sub-chain with a 0x60000000 (DMA ret) tag on both tails, then re-links via 0x20000000 (next) tags pointing at the new +0x118, updating +0x128/+0x12C with mapped addresses (| ctx+0x124).

name: gfx_select_list
summary: Switches the packet writer between the two interleaved chains (VIF1/GIF or ctx0/ctx1): if the target differs from byte ctx+3 (and MSKPATH3 state 0x1C0/0x1B8 allows), appends a 0x20000000 (next) tag to the other chain tail (+0x128/+0x12C) pointing at the new current position, swaps the saved masks +0xF8/+0x100/+0x108, stores new tail, returns previous selection.

name: gfx_sync_pipeline
summary: Full render-path sync with forced recovery: gfx_dma_sync(1) and (2); poll VIF1_STAT (0x10003C00) & 0x1F000003 until clear (timeout 0x1000000 -> write 1 to VIF1_FBRST 0x10003C10); poll VU1 busy via cfc2 VPU-STAT ($29) & 0x100 (timeout -> ctc2 FBRST |= 0x200 force-break); poll GIF_STAT (0x10003020) & 0xC00 (timeout -> GIF_CTRL (0x10003000)=1, GIF_MODE (0x10003010)=4). Polyphony's sceGsSyncPath equivalent.

name: gfx_wait_vblank_event
summary: Sleeps until the 64-bit vblank counter at 0x1048180 changes: links a stack node {next, tid=GetThreadId} into the vsync waiter list at 0x10481C0 under DI/EI, SleepThread-loops until the counter differs, unlinks, CancelWakeupThread. Woken by the VBlank INTC handler (F_0100E630).

name: gfx_vsync
summary: n==0: returns the current vblank count (u64 @0x1048180). n>0: waits (F_0100D8D0) until count-lastSync(+8) >= n; n<0: only waits if fewer than |n| vblanks have elapsed, returns 1 if no wait needed. Updates lastSync (+8) and the field byte ctx+0x1BC (from 0x1048194 when interlaced). Called by main, F_01000880, F_010049C8, F_01004F58, F_01005458 — the frame pacing primitive of the startup screen.
sig: long gfx_vsync(int n /* 0=query, >0 wait n, <0 throttle */)

name: gfx_set_draw_buffer
summary: Sets the draw environment in the SPR context: FBP = addr>>11 (+0x80), FBW = (w+63)>>6 (+0x82), PSM (+0x83), XYOFFSET = (0x800-w/2)<<4 / (0x800-h/2)<<4 (+0x194/+0x196 and +0x88/+0x8C), size fields +0x184/+0x188/+0x18C/+0x190/+0x192, dirty flags +0xE8 |= 0x30003, clears +0x23; then jumps into the follow-on draw-area setter at 0x0100DB88 with (0,0,w,h) which fills +0x1AC..+0x1B8 and tail-calls F_0100DBB8 (next chunk). Caller F_01000B40.

name: gs_update_scissor_and_viewport

Entered only via tail-jump `j` from 0x0100DBB0 (window-set function in previous chunk).

name: gs_set_clear_color
summary: Stores a0 into GS context word 0x7000314C; that word is used as the RGBAQ color of the buffer-clear packet built by F_0100DD10 (via F_0100DE80). Caller: F_01000B40 (startup-screen main loop).

name: gs_build_clear_packet
summary: Appends to the ctx packet buffer (+0x118) a DMAtag(cnt)+VIF1{FLUSH,DIRECT}+GIFtag(4x A+D: TEST_1=0x47:=a1, ZBUF_1=0x4E from cache+0x98/psm byte +0x1D0, PRIM=6 sprite, RGBAQ=a2|Q=1.0) followed by a second GIFtag (PRE, regs 0xD5=XYZ3/XYZ2) drawing sprites in 0x400-subpixel (64px) columns across target tgt at depth a3 - the classic GS framebuffer clear.

name: gs_clear_buffers
summary: Flushes dirty GS regs (F_0100E570); mask bit0/bit1 select a clear of target ctx+0x184 with TEST=0x32001 or 0, color=[ctx+0x14C], Z=(int)([0x154]*[0x160]); mask bit2 re-emits FRAME/SCISSOR/XYOFFSET of target ctx+0x170 (F_0100DF40) then clears it with color=[ctx+0x150], Z=0. Caller F_01000B40.

name: gs_emit_render_target_regs
summary: Builds a GIFtag with 3 A+D pairs: FRAME_1(0x4C) from descriptor bytes +0x170..+0x173, SCISSOR_1(0x40) from cached +0xA0 x/y divided by divisors +0x188/+0x18C (uses both EE pipes: div/div1, mult3/mult1; break-on-zero divisor), XYOFFSET_1(0x18) from +0x17C/+0x17E; sets dirty +0xE8|=0x13.

name: gs_build_image_transfer_packet
summary: Builds a host->local GS transfer: A+D BITBLTBUF(0x50)=img[0], TRXPOS(0x51), TRXREG(0x52), TRXDIR(0x53)=0, then an IMAGE-mode GIFtag; qword count computed from pixel count scaled by PSM via jump table at 0x103e520 indexed by img byte+3 (32/24/16/8/4 bpp cases). Returns qwc. Caller F_0100BD38 (startup texture upload).
sig: u32 gs_build_image_transfer_packet(qword *pkt, GsImageDesc *img, u32 dx, u32 dy, u32 trxreg_wh, u32 dir, u32 qwc_hint?)

name: float_to_gs_param_encode
summary: Successively compares f12 against 64.0,32.0,...(10 halvings) accumulating a bit code, 4-bit-reverses the low nibble and returns code|(clamped_step<<16). Custom float->fixed encoding consumed by the kind-0xB scalar parameter path of F_0100EFF0; exact GS target format unresolved. Callers F_0100C158/F_0100C230/F_0100EFF0.

name: float_pow_fixed44 (hidden, dead)

name: gs_draw_textured_bg_sprite
summary: Flushes dirty regs (F_0100E570) then appends DMAtag(qwc=4)+VIF1{FLUSH,DIRECT 4}+REGLIST GIFtag (NREG=6, regs 0x43C310 = PRIM,RGBAQ,UV,XYZ3,UV,XYZ2): PRIM=ctx[+4]|0x116 (sprite+TME+FST), colors from ctx+0x16C and +0xB64 (bg blend color), corner coords offset by +0x1AC/+0x1B0/+0x190/+0x192 in 12.4 subpixels (shift 3 or 4 selected by AA byte +0x23). Draws the warning-screen background quad.

name: gs_init_vu0_constants
summary: Six COP2 macro-mode ops (vsub vf28/vf29:=0, vmove/viadd-style setup of VU0 regs used by the color->float conversion in F_0100EFF0), then sets ctx byte+0=1 (initialized flag). Caller F_0100C050 (display init).

name: gs_get_display_state
summary: Returns 0 unless state byte 0x104821B==1; then 9 if ctx+0x1BD set, else 4 if signed byte ctx+0x1BC nonzero else 3. Some mode/progress query for the boot screen; caller F_01000C88. Meaning of codes unresolved.

name: gs_set_bg_color_f
summary: Loads f15=1.0/f16=255.0, packs the four floats to u32 RGBA via F_0100EDB0, then tail-jumps the u32 setter at 0x0100ED58. Caller F_01000B40.
sig: u32 gs_set_bg_color_f(float r, float g, float b, float a)

name: lcg_rand
summary: Classic LCG: state@0x1041e34 = state*0x5D588B65 + 1 (multiplier is the well-known PS2-era rand constant); returns new state sign-extended. Only caller: the XOR descrambler F_0100E4E8.

name: xor_unscramble_with_lcg
summary: One-shot (guard byte 0x1041e30): XORs len bytes at buf with successive lcg_rand() low bytes. Called once (0x0100C5B0) with (0x1034730, 0x3DA8): descrambles the embedded startup-screen GS display-list data in .data (the high-entropy block 0x1034730..0x10384D8 in datamap). Light obfuscation, not cryptographic verification.

name: gs_flush_all_regs (hidden, dead)
summary: Unheadered thunk between F_0100E4E8 and F_0100E570: sets the full dirty mask 0x03FF1FFF1FFF (10 general + 13 ctx1 + 13 ctx2 bits) into ctx+0xE8 then tail-jumps gs_flush_dirty_regs. No references found - dead.

name: gs_flush_dirty_regs
summary: If display disabled (hword ctx+0x1BE==0) just clears dirty mask +0xE8. Else reserves 16B, emits changed regs via F_0100EE80, and wraps them as DMAtag(id=cnt,qwc=n+1) + VIF1 {FLUSH, DIRECT n+1} + GIFtag(nloop=n,EOP,A+D); advances write ptr +0x118 by n*16+0x20. Proves the driver renders through VIF1/PATH2 DMA chains.

name: intc_vblank_handler
summary: Installed by AddIntcHandler(2=INTC_VBLANK_S,...) at 0x0100C5C4. Reads+clears COP0 reg25 perf counters (sel1/sel3) accumulating u64s at 0x10481C8/0x10481D0; samples GS_CSR(0x12001000) FIELD bit13 into +0x14; increments u64 frame counter 0x1048180; invokes user vsync callback [+0x10](count); iSignalSema-like (F_0101C7E0) every {next,semaId} node of list +0x40 and the three per-channel lists +0x20+i*0xC; sync/ei; returns 1.

name: intc_vif1_handler (hidden)
summary: Unheadered function currently glued to F_0100E630; installed by AddIntcHandler(5=INTC_VIF1, &0x100E770) at 0x0100C5D8. Checks VIF1_STAT(0x10003C00) bit11 and VIF1_CODE(0x10003C80) mark bits 0x40000/0x10000/0x20000 to classify the i-bit interrupt; adjusts counters 0x1048196..98, resumes VIF1 via FBRST(0x10003C10)=8 (STC) or restarts GIF (0x1000A000 CHCR|=0x100, QWC=0); sync/ei; returns 1.

name: intc_gs_finish_handler
summary: Installed by AddIntcHandler(0=INTC_GS). Writes GS_CSR(0x12001000)=2 to clear FINISH, increments finish counter byte 0x1048195; when it reaches 2 begins the GS->EE readback via F_0100EB00 (two-FINISH handshake for local->host image download).

name: dmac_channel_handler
summary: Installed by AddDmacHandler for ch 0,1,2 at 0x0100CBA4.. Reads CHCR via base table 0x10394D8 {0x10008000 VIF0, 0x10009000 VIF1, 0x1000A000 GIF}; on end-of-chain (tag id 7, or 6 with ASP=0) clears busy byte 0x1048180+0x1D+ch*0xC and signals waiter semaphore list +0x20+ch*0xC via F_0101C7E0; tag-IRQ sets flag +0x1C+ch; ch1 drives the FINISH/readback sequence (counter +0x15 -> F_0100EB00/F_0100EB78); ch2 manages counters +0x16..+0x18, restarts GIF (CHCR|=0x100 at 0x1000A000) and VIF1 via FBRST(0x10003C10)=8.

name: gs_readback_begin
summary: Reads the pseudo download record pointed by D1_TADR (VIF1 DMA 0x10009000+0x30): {u16 qwc, u32 madr, cbk, arg}; saves record ptr at st+0x44; sets GS BUSDIR(0x12001040)=1 and VIF1_STAT(0x10003C00).FDR=0x800000 (reverse FIFO); programs D1 MADR/QWC and CHCR=(CHCR&~0x10F)|0x100 (to-memory, start): local->host image download begins.

name: gs_readback_end
summary: Invokes the record's completion callback rec[8](rec[4] madr, rec[0xC] arg); clears BUSDIR(0x12001040)=0 and VIF1_STAT FDR; D1_QWC=0, D1_TADR=rec+0x10 and CHCR=(CHCR&0xFEF0)|0x105 to resume the VIF1 source chain past the download record; restarts GIF (0x1000A000 CHCR|=0x100).

name: dma_start_source_chain
summary: Waits/preps via F_0100CCB8, sets per-channel busy flag [0x1048180+ch*0xC+0x1D]=1, then via base table 0x10394D8 programs QWC=0, TADR=tadr (bit31 SPR set when tadr is in scratchpad 0x70000000) and CHCR=(CHCR&0xFEC0)|0x105 (source chain, start). Kicks the frame packet built in scratchpad. Callers F_0100CF28/F_0100CFE8.

name: gs_compute_display_period (hidden)
summary: Unheadered function inside F_0100EC20's region, tail-called (j 0x100ecd0) from the video-mode setter at 0x0100D2DC/0x0100D2F4 (chunk 4): ctx+8 = 0x320, or 0x33E when PAL byte ctx+0x25 set, adjusted +0xA/+0x14/0 by interlace/frame mode words ctx+0x1C4/+0x1C8; 0 when mode==3.

name: gs_set_bg_color (hidden)
summary: Unheadered function tail-called from F_0100E478 (j 0x100ed58): stores rgba at ctx+0xB60, derives a scaled/blended copy into +0xB64 (MMI byte ops, ~(a1*129)>>8 with top byte preserved), and when immediate-update byte ctx+0x22 is set tail-calls gs_set_color_param([0xB6C] mask, [0xB68] slot, color).

name: pack_rgba_floats_to_u32
summary: Scales f12..f14 by f16 (255.0), f15 by 128.0 (GS alpha 0x80=1.0), rounds (+0.5), clamps [0,255] via EE max.s/min.s (the <bad>-decoded 0x27/0x28/0x29 COP1 functs), converts and packs r|g<<8|b<<16|a<<24.
sig: u32 pack_rgba_floats_to_u32(float r,float g,float b,float a, float scale /*f16*/)

name: gs_emit_masked_regs
summary: For each set bit of a1 appends one A+D pair {shadow value (16B stride, a3), GS register number from byte list a2}; advances a2 per bit position. Register-number lists live at 0x1039510 (general: COLCLAMP,DIMX,DTHE,FOGCOL,PABE,PRMODECONT,SCANMSK,TEXA,TEXCLUT,TEXFLUSH), 0x1039520 (context-1 regs), 0x1039530 (context-2 regs).
sig: qword* gs_emit_masked_regs(qword *out, u64 bitmask, const u8 *reglist, const qword *shadow)

name: gs_collect_dirty_regs
summary: mask = dirty(+0xE8) & enabled(+0xF8); clears those bits from +0xE8, ORs into ever-set +0xF0; emits general regs (mask bits 32..41, shadows +0x30), ctx1 (bits 0..12, shadows +0x80), ctx2 (bits 16..28) via F_0100EE48 with the three byte tables; returns pair count. Core of the shadowed/dirty GS state machine.

name: gs_store_param_quad
summary: Jump table at 0x103e5e0: stores the 128-bit register $7 (packed 4 floats) into ctx + context*0x50 + slot {+0x960,+0x970,both,+0x980,+0x990} selected by kind; sets ctx+0x20|=4 (params dirty). The listing's '0x103ef40 .rodata' annotations on the sq instructions are bogus (base register is computed, not the literal).
sig: void gs_store_param_quad(GsCtx *ctx /*t0*/, int context, int kind /*<5*/) /*value in $7 quad*/

name: gs_set_color_param
summary: kind==0xB: converts value to float (val/128?), stores float+0 + encoded form (F_0100E198) into scalar slots +0x9A0/+0x9AC (mask&1) and +0x9F0/+0x9FC (mask&2). Other kinds: converts u32 RGBA to 4 floats via VU0 macro ops with constant 0x3B808081 (=1/255.0f) and stores through F_0100EF50 for each context in mask. Reached from bg-color setter 0x0100ED58 and F_0100C158/F_0100C230.
sig: void gs_set_color_param(int ctxmask, int kind, u32 value)

name: mc_close_sync
summary: WaitSema on game MC lock (gp var 0x1041e38); retries sceMcClose (F_01015C88; libmc RPC fno=3 observed in its disasm) with yield F_0100F640 until accepted; blocks in mc_sync_wait (F_0100F4D8); SignalSema via F_0100F198; returns the mcserv result. Callers F_01005458/F_01005748 (MCard source/FileName code).

name: mc_unlock (tail stub)
summary: Loads MC lock sema id (0x1041e38) in the delay slot and jumps the SignalSema helper F_0100F6B0.

name: mc_shutdown
summary: If the MC lock semaphore id (0x1041e38) is >=0, DeleteSema (F_0101BBF0) and reset it to -1. Caller F_010009D8 (cleanup path before launching core.gt3).

name: mc_getdir_sync
summary: Blocking wrapper of sceMcGetDir (F_01016478: RPC fno=0xD, 0x400-byte path copy, table cache-flush of maxent*0x40 bytes - matches Sony libmc 2.2 GetDir exactly) under the MC lock, with retry+yield and mc_sync_wait. Caller F_01005458.
sig: int mc_getdir_sync(int port, int slot, const char *name, u32 mode, int maxent, sceMcTblGetDir *table)

name: mc_unlock (tail stub #2)
summary: Identical 2-instruction stub to F_0100F198 (one per caller object): jumps SignalSema helper F_0100F6B0 with the MC lock sema id.

name: mc_getinfo_sync
summary: Blocking wrapper of sceMcGetInfo (F_010162F0: RPC fno=1, stores the three out-pointers at 0x1048968.. and registers RPC-done copy-back stub 0x1016298 - Sony libmc GetInfo shape) under MC lock; retry+yield, then mc_sync_wait. Caller F_010053C8.
sig: int mc_getinfo_sync(int port, int slot, int *type, int *free, int *format)

name: mc_unlock (tail stub #3)
summary: Same SignalSema tail stub as F_0100F198.

name: mc_init_once
summary: If MC lock sema (0x1041e38) <0: creates it via create_mutex_sema(1) (F_0100F5D0), WaitSema, then loops sceMcInit (F_010157B8) with yield until it returns 0, and unlocks via the 0x100F3A0 stub (tail jump). Caller F_01000880 (boot init).

name: mc_init_once_unlock (tail stub #4)
summary: Same SignalSema tail stub as F_0100F198; mc_init_once's own (split off in matching round 3, ref/extra_starts.txt).

name: mc_open_sync
summary: Blocking wrapper of F_01015B18 = sceMcOpen (4 args, name null-checked, libmc state after 'PsIIlibmc 2240' @0x103BE78; mcserv fno 2 numbering) under MC lock; retry+yield then mc_sync_wait; returns the fd from the sync result. Callers F_01005458/F_01005748 (MCardSource/MCardFileName).
sig: int mc_open_sync(int port, int slot, const char *name, int mode)

name: mc_unlock (tail stub #4)
summary: Same SignalSema tail stub as F_0100F198.

name: mc_read_sync
summary: Blocking wrapper of F_01015EA8 = sceMcRead (3 args; callee does SifWriteBackDCache of the user buffer, mcserv fno 5 numbering) under MC lock; retry+yield then mc_sync_wait; returns bytes read from sync result. Callers F_01005458/F_01005748.
sig: int mc_read_sync(int fd, void *buf, int size)

name: mc_unlock (tail stub #5)
summary: Same SignalSema tail stub as F_0100F198.

name: mc_sync_wait
summary: Loops sceMcSync(0, cmd, result) (F_010161B8, which polls sceSifCheckStatRpc F_0101E480 and reports libmc current-command word 0x103be88) with yield F_0100F640 until it returns 1 (command finished).

name: strlen
summary: EE-optimized 128-bit strlen: lq of the aligned qword, mask to ignore bytes before s (dsllv of -1 by (s&0xF)*8, pexew-style swap when offset>=8), pceqb against zero per qword, then dsub/xor/dsll/plzcw to locate the first NUL byte. Game-provided strlen that also satisfies libmc's reference (called from 0x10165D0) - overrides the libc archive copy.

name: create_mutex_sema
summary: CreateSema (F_0101BBE0) with param struct {max=1, init=a0, option=0} on stack; on -1 yields (F_0100F640) and retries; on 0 recurses once. Returns sema id. Used for both the MC lock (0x1041e38) and the host-I/O lock (0x1041e60, via F_01012F68).

name: yield_low_priority
summary: GetThreadId (F_0101BAD0), ReferThreadStatus (F_0101BAE0), ChangeThreadPriority(self, 0x7E) (F_0101BA70), then 100 iterations of {busy delay F_0100F8D8(10); RotateThreadReadyQueue(0x7E) (F_0101BA90)}, finally restores the original priority from status+0x18. Lets the IOP/RPC threads run while the boot loader polls.

name: signal_sema_helper
summary: Reads COP0 Status (result unused - probably vestigial i/SignalSema selection) then calls SignalSema (F_0101BC10). Shared unlock tail for the MC lock stubs and host-I/O unlock F_01012FA0.

name: host_open
summary: Takes the host-I/O mutex (0x1041e60 via F_01012F68), calls the SIF fileio client sceOpen (F_0101F1B8, libkernl region; used for 'host:' paths - string @0x1041E18), releases lock (F_01012FA0). Returns fd. Callers F_01005970/F_01005A78 (HostSource/HostFileName).

name: host_lseek
summary: Locked wrapper around sceLseek (F_0101F5C0). Used with whence=2 (SEEK_END) by host_get_file_size.
sig: int host_lseek(int fd, int offset, int whence)

name: host_read
summary: Locked wrapper around sceRead (F_0101F7F8). Caller F_01005970 (HostSource::read path).
sig: int host_read(int fd, void *buf, int len)

name: host_write
summary: Locked wrapper around sceWrite (F_0101FA68). Caller F_01005A78.
sig: int host_write(int fd, const void *buf, int len)

name: host_close
summary: Locked wrapper around sceClose (F_0101F440).

name: host_get_file_size
summary: fd=host_open(path, 1=O_RDONLY); if <0 returns -1; size=host_lseek(fd,0,SEEK_END); host_close(fd); out[0]=0x11 (status/type code), out[1]=size; returns 0. Backs HostFileName::stat-style callers F_01005B08/F_01005B68.
sig: int host_get_file_size(const char *path, struct {int status; int size;} *out)

name: busy_wait_delay
summary: Pure spin: iterates about n*75 times through a nop-padded loop (n*5*15 computed with dsll/dsubu). Used by yield_low_priority.

name: pdistd::Allocator::Allocator(int)
summary: Zeroes first/end/+8/freeHead, stores flag at +0x10, sets vptr(+0x14)=0x103e680 (.rodata vtable adjacent to RTTI name 'Q26pdistd9Allocator' @0x103E690). Called from static-init thunk F_01011480 (vtable-ish record 0x1026ca0).

name: pdistd::Allocator::Allocator(void*, unsigned int, int)
summary: Stores flag(+0x10) and vptr, then assigns the heap range via F_0100FB40(base,size).

name: pdistd::Allocator::~Allocator(void)
summary: GCC2.9x dtor: restores vptr=0x103e680, clears list fields (inlined reset), calls operator delete (F_01019910) when flag&1. Sits in the .rodata vtable at 0x103e68c (only virtual besides the RTTI slot __tf at 0x103e684) - matching Lupo2's 24-byte _vt$Q26pdistd9Allocator.

name: pdistd::Allocator::alignRepStart
summary: Aligns rep payload (rep+0x10) up to align: already aligned -> return rep; gap <0x20 -> relocates the 16-byte Rep header to alignedPtr-0x10 fixing neighbor links and address-order in the free chain; else splits via insertRepAt (F_0100FAA8) + pushFreeRep (F_0100FAF8). Used by allocate.

name: pdistd::Allocator::rebuildHeadRep
summary: Re-forms the heap's first Rep (this[0]) spanning to rep->next: this[8]=first, first->prev=0, first->next=rep->next, fixes backlink if next<end. Used by free() when the freed block merges to the heap head.

name: pdistd::Allocator::insertRepAt
summary: Creates a new Rep header at rep+offset, links it into the address-ordered chain between rep and rep->next (fixing the next block's prev if within heap end); returns the new Rep. The block-split primitive.

name: pdistd::Allocator::unlinkRep
summary: Coalescing primitive: rep->next = victim->next, and if victim->next < end fixes its prev backlink to rep - removes victim from the address-ordered chain.

name: pdistd::Allocator::pushFreeRep
summary: Head-inserts rep on the doubly-linked free list at this[0xC]: rep->prevFree=0, rep->nextFree=oldHead, oldHead->prevFree=rep.

name: pdistd::Allocator::removeFreeRep
summary: Unlinks rep from the free list (this[0xC] head), patching prevFree/nextFree neighbors.

name: pdistd::Allocator::assign
summary: Aligns base up and size down to 16; sets first=this[0]=this[8]=freeHead=alignedBase, end=this[4]=base+size; initializes the single spanning free Rep {prev=0,next=end,prevFree=0,nextFree=0}. Called by the (base,size,flag) ctor and by the heap-manager F_01011210 (chunk 6).

name: pdistd::Allocator::unassign
summary: Zeroes freeHead/first/end/+8 (with a dead load of this[0]). Twin of reset() from the main allocator.cxx object; unreferenced in this build (kept via the vtable/metadata record at 0x1039648).

name: pdistd::Allocator::allocate
summary: di() guard (F_01012F38 returns prior EIE); align=max(align,0x10); need=alignUp(size,align)+0x10; best-fit scan of the free list accounting alignment slack; removeFreeRep, alignRepStart, split remainder >=need+0x20 via insertRepAt+pushFreeRep; marks block allocated by prevFree=nextFree=0xFFFFFFFF; conditional ei; returns rep+0x10 or NULL. Called by the operator-new-style front-ends F_01011320/F_01011390/F_01011410 (chunk 6).

name: pdistd::Allocator::reallocate
summary: NULL ptr -> allocate. Validates Rep(ptr-0x10) range+allocated magic; under di() tries in-place resize: absorbs the following free Rep (removeFreeRep + unlinkRep/insertRepAt, re-splitting if >= need+0x30); else allocates new, memcpy (F_0101B010) old payload, free (F_0100FED8). Front-end F_010113C8 (realloc).
sig: void* Allocator::reallocate(void *ptr, u32 size, u32 align)

name: pdistd::Allocator::free
summary: Validates Rep(ptr-0x10) bounds and 0xFFFFFFFF/0xFFFFFFFF allocated magic; under di() coalesces with the previous Rep if free (removeFreeRep+unlinkRep, or rebuildHeadRep when prev==0) and with the following Rep if free; pushFreeRep; conditional ei. Front-end F_01011368 (operator delete path, 11 callers).

name: pdistd::Allocator::getMaxFreeSize
summary: Under di(): walks the free list taking max(rep->next - rep); returns max-0x10 (largest allocatable payload). Wrapped by F_010112A0.

name: pdistd::Allocator::getTotalFreeSize
summary: Under di(): sums (rep->next - rep - 0x10) over the free list. Wrapped by F_010112C0.

name: pdistd::Allocator::debug
summary: Prints heap dump via printf front-end F_01011678 using the 'Allocator::debug' format @0x103E5F8 (CONTEXT anchor) plus fmts @0x103e620/0x103e638/0x103e668: header (first/end), one line per Rep in the address chain {rep, next, size, prevFree, nextFree}, footer; di/ei guarded.

name: pdistd::Allocator::countAllocatedReps
summary: Under di(): walks the address-ordered chain in [first,end) counting Reps whose prevFree==0xFFFFFFFF and nextFree==0xFFFFFFFF (allocated marker). Wrapped by F_01011300.

name: pdistd::Allocator::repValid(pdistd::Allocator::Rep*)
summary: Exact match of Lupo2 symbol repValid__Q26pdistd9AllocatorPQ36pdistd9Allocator3Rep (64B there / 72B here): rep within [this[0], this[4]) and rep->prevFree==0xFFFFFFFF and ~rep->nextFree==0.

name: pdistd::Allocator::reset(void)
summary: Zeroes freeHead/first/end/+8. Matches Lupo2 reset__Q26pdistd9Allocator (20B) and sits in the same {repValid, reset, __tf} object cluster as Lupo2.

name: __tfQ26pdistd9Allocator (typeinfo function for pdistd::Allocator)
summary: Lazily constructs the static type_info at 0x1041ea0 (gp-0x7e50) from RTTI name 'Q26pdistd9Allocator' @0x103E690 via F_01019C58 (__user_type_info/type_info ctor). Referenced from the vtable RTTI slot at 0x103e684. Matches Lupo2 __tfQ26pdistd9Allocator.

name: pdistd::PrintFormatTargetBase::PrintFormatTargetBase(void)
summary: Sets vptr(+0)=0x103fc60. That .rodata vtable's slots: +4 = __tf F_010111D0 (typeinfo fn for RTTI name 'Q26pdistd21PrintFormatTargetBase' @0x103FC78), +0xC = dtor F_01010330, +0x14 = default output virtual F_01010360. Called from thunk F_010114A8 (printf.cxx front-end).

name: pdistd::PrintFormatTargetBase::~PrintFormatTargetBase(void)
summary: Restores vptr=0x103fc60; operator delete (F_01019910) when flag&1. In vtable slot 0x103fc6c.

name: pdistd::PrintFormatTargetBase::putc (default)
summary: Two-instruction virtual returning 0; occupies vtable slot +0x14 (0x103fc74) - exactly the {delta@+0x10, pfn@+0x14} slot that the PrintFormat engine invokes per output character (derived classes like printf.cxx/vsprintf.cxx PrintTarget override it).

name: pdistd::PrintFormat (printf format engine)
summary: 3688-byte %-format interpreter (the flagged 'largest function' of this chunk): flag chars via jump table 0x103fb40, width/precision incl '*', h/l/L modifiers, conversion dispatch table 0x103fb90 ('E'..'x'): %c %d %i %u %o %x/X (digit tables 0x103fb20/0x103fb30), %s (uses '(null)' @0x1041E40), %p, and %e/%f/%g by manual IEEE-754 double decomposition (exp>>52, mantissa|implicit bit) against the u64 powers-of-ten table @0x103fa80. Every character goes through the target's virtual putc (vtable +0x10 delta/+0x14 fn, this+delta), aborting on -1; returns chars written. Args are 8-byte va slots. Sole caller F_010115D8 (printf/vsprintf front-end, chunk 6).

name: typeinfo function for pdistd::PrintFormatTargetBase (__tfQ26pdistd21PrintFormatTargetBase)
summary: Lazy-constructs the static type_info at 0x1041ea8 (.sbss) via F_01019C58(__user_type_info ctor) with name string 'Q26pdistd21PrintFormatTargetBase' @0x103fc78. Referenced from PrintFormatTargetBase vtable slot 0 (0x103fc64). Matches Lupo2 symbol 0x002D73D8.

name: heap_init_once
summary: One-time heap arena setup guarded by DIntr clone F_01012F38/ei: if flag 0x1041e50 is 0, base=align16(_end@0x1041e58=0x104DE94), top=0x01F00000@0x1041e5c, memset(base,0,size) via F_0101B1B8, then registers the arena with the global pdistd::Allocator at 0x1048240 via F_0100FB40; stores base/size at 0x1041e50/54. Called by all malloc-family wrappers.

name: heap_max_free_size
summary: Wrapper calling F_01010010 on the global Allocator 0x1048240: walks the free list at Allocator+0xc and returns the largest free block size minus 0x10 (header). Unreferenced in this binary (only eh_frame xref 0x1039990).

name: heap_total_free_size
summary: Wrapper calling F_01010078 on the global Allocator: sums (blocksize-0x10) over the free list, i.e. total free bytes. Unreferenced.

name: heap_dump
summary: Wrapper calling F_010100E0 on the global Allocator; that routine iterates the heap under DIntr and prints via Polyphony printf F_01011678 (Allocator::debug format @0x103e5f8 region). Unreferenced.

name: heap_check
summary: Wrapper calling F_010101D8 on the global Allocator: walks blocks between Allocator+0 (base) and +4 (end) validating/measuring the arena under DIntr guard. Exact semantic (verify vs. used-bytes) uncertain. Unreferenced.

name: calloc
summary: heap_init_once, then F_0100FBB8(globalAllocator, nmemb*size (mult/mflo), align=0x10). calloc-shaped (two args multiplied); no explicit memset seen here, so zeroing (if any) is inside the Allocator. Unreferenced in this binary.

name: free
summary: If ptr!=NULL calls F_0100FED8(globalAllocator@0x1048240, ptr). Called by operator delete (F_01019910) and by game/ImageLoader code (11 callers).

name: malloc
summary: heap_init_once then F_0100FBB8(globalAllocator, size, 0x10). 12 callers including operator-new path (F_01019988) and game code.

name: realloc
summary: heap_init_once then F_0100FD10(globalAllocator, ptr, size, 0x10). One caller (F_01000FB8, game code).

name: memalign
summary: heap_init_once then F_0100FBB8(globalAllocator, size=a1, align=a0). Callers F_01000A50 (main-area, allocates the core.gt3 inflate buffers) and F_01005458.

name: _GLOBAL_$D$ (static destructor: global pdistd::Allocator)
summary: Calls Allocator dtor F_0100F978(0x1048240, 2) (flag 2 = no delete). Listed in the __DTOR_LIST__-style table at 0x1026cb0 {3, F_01003C90, this, F_01000108}.

name: _GLOBAL_$I$ (static constructor: global pdistd::Allocator)

sig: int sceSifLoadElfPart(const char *name, const char *secname, sceExecData *data)

name: sceSifGetIopAddr
summary: LOADFILE fno 3 (GET_ADDR): reads a byte(0)/half(1)/word(2) from IOP memory; sends {addr,width} (0x20), recv 0x20, stores the value into *out; invalid width returns 0xfffefffe. Sony public name for this loadfile peek is uncertain.
sig: int sceSifGetIopAddr(unsigned int iop_addr, void *out, int width)

name: sceSifSetIopAddr

sig: int sceSifSetIopAddr(unsigned int iop_addr, const void *value, int width)

name: sceSifResetIop
summary: Low-level IOP reset (ps2sdk SifIopReset equivalent): builds SifCmdResetData @0x104d880 {psize=0x68, fid=0x80000003, arglen@+0x10, mode@+0x14, arg[0x50]@+0x18}, stops SIF (F_0101BEB0), WriteBackDCache, DMA to IOP MAINADDR (sceSifGetReg(0x80000000)) via sceSifSetDma (F_0101BFA0), then sceSifSetReg(4,0x10000 SIFINIT), (4,0x20000 CMDINIT), (0x80000002,0), (0x80000000,0).

name: sceSifIopIsAlive
summary: Returns (sceSifGetReg(SIF_REG_SMFLAG=4) & 0x10000 SIF_STAT_SIFINIT) != 0 — 'SIF initialized' probe. No callers in this binary.

name: sceSifSyncIop
summary: Polls SMFLAG bit 0x40000 (SIF_STAT_BOOTEND); when set, acknowledges it via sceSifSetReg(4,0x40000), re-initializes the DECI2 TTY (F_01022C40) and returns 1, else 0. Called from game code F_01000880 to wait for the IOPRP224.IMG reboot.

name: sceSifRebootIop
summary: Builds "rom0:UDNL " (prefix @0x1040720) on the stack; if strlen(img)+11 > 0x50 prints "too long parameter '%s'" @0x1040730 via printf (F_01011678 — the game's Polyphony printf, linked as extern) and returns 0; else sceSifInitRpc(0) (F_0101DA50), F_0101DBF0 (RPC/queue teardown), then F_010228B8(str, 0). Called from F_01000880 with the IOPRP path.

name: DIntr
summary: Classic EE DIntr: reads COP0 Status, if EIE (bit 16) set, executes di + sync.p in a loop until EIE clears; returns whether interrupts were previously enabled. Called from 23 places incl. game code.

name: EIntr
summary: EE EIntr: samples Status.EIE then executes ei; returns previous enable state.

name: SetSyscall
summary: Raw EE kernel syscall wrapper: li v1,0x74; syscall — syscall 116 = SetSyscall.

name: clear_user_syscalls
summary: for (i=0x80; i<0x100; i++) SetSyscall(i, 0) — clears all user-definable syscall slots at program start. Called only from _InitSys.

name: _InitSys
summary: The libkernl startup hook called directly by crt0 (F_01000008): clears user syscalls 0x80-0xFF, calls F_0101C558 (alarm/intr handler init cluster) and tail-jumps to F_0101C708. Matches the _InitSys call in Sony's crt0.s.

name: tty_reinit_after_iop_reset
summary: Clears the DECI2-TTY-initialized flag @0x103dadc and tail-jumps to the TTY init F_010235B8 (re-opens the DECI2 TTY protocol after the IOP, and thus the DECI2 manager, was reset). Called from sceSifSyncIop.

name: F_01022C50
summary: SPLIT-OFF (boundary fix): missed function start at 0x01022C50 after F_01022C40's tail-jump: busy-wait for INTC VBON — writes 4

name: wait_vblank_get_csr
summary: Calls F_0101BF50(&flag, &out) (SetVSyncFlag-style kernel call), acknowledges INTC_STAT (0x1000F000) bit 2 (VBON), polls until VBON or the kernel-set flag, re-acks, returns the 64-bit value (GS CSR at vsync) the kernel stored. No callers — dead library code.

name: write
summary: libc syscall glue: only fd 1/2 (stdout/stderr) accepted, else -1; lazily initializes the DECI2 TTY (flag @0x103dadc, init F_010235B8) then forwards to the TTY write F_01023398(buf, nbytes). This is how all bootstrap printf output reaches DECI2 TTY.
sig: int write(int fd, const void *buf, size_t nbytes)

name: read
summary: libc glue: only fd 0 (stdin); lazy TTY init then F_010234E8(buf, nbytes) which drains the TTY receive ring.
sig: int read(int fd, void *buf, size_t nbytes)

name: open_stub
summary: libc glue stub: sets *__errno() (F_01026940) = 5 (EIO) and returns -1. Position (right after read) suggests open; could equally be lseek. Followed by three headerless 2-instruction stubs returning -1 (close/lseek/etc.).

name: stub_ret_minus1_a
summary: MISSED-BY-DETECTOR 2-instruction stub: jr ra; li v0,-1. One of close/lseek/ioctl-style unsupported libc syscalls.

name: stub_ret_minus1_b

sig: int lseek(int fd, int off, int whence)

name: stub_ret_minus1_c
summary: MISSED-BY-DETECTOR stub returning -1 (third of three).

name: sbrk
summary: Program-break allocator: break variable @0x103dae0 initialized to _end (0x104DE94); DIntr-protected; new break checked against EndOfHeap (syscall wrapper F_0101BBC0); on overflow sets *__errno()=0xC (ENOMEM) and returns -1, else returns old break. Backs the bootstrap malloc/Allocator heap.

name: getpid
summary: MISSED-BY-DETECTOR stub: jr ra; li v0,1 — returns pid 1, pairs with kill() below.

name: fstat
summary: MISSED-BY-DETECTOR stub: st->st_mode = 0x2000 (S_IFCHR, character device), 64-bit size field at +0x48 zeroed, returns 0 — standard newlib glue telling stdio that fds are TTYs.

name: isatty
summary: MISSED-BY-DETECTOR stub: returns 1 (everything is a TTY).

name: kill
summary: If pid==1 calls F_0101B800 — the same Exit routine crt0 jumps to with main's result — with sig as status; else returns 0. Classic newlib kill glue paired with getpid()==1.

name: link_stub
summary: Stub: *__errno()=5 (EIO), return -1. One of the tail pair of unsupported libc syscalls (link/unlink or stat/times); identical body to F_01022F50.

name: unlink_stub
summary: Stub: *__errno()=5 (EIO), return -1; identical to F_01022F28.

name: sceDeci2Open
summary: Deci2Call(1, {protocol, opt, handler, &status}) via F_0101C010 (syscall 0x7C wrapper); passes the kernel status block 0x104d8e8 through the uncached mirror (|0x20000000). Standard EE kernel DECI2 glue, matches ps2sdk layout exactly.
sig: int sceDeci2Open(unsigned short protocol, void *opt, void (*handler)(int event, int param, void *opt))

name: sceDeci2Close
summary: Deci2Call(2, {s}).

name: sceDeci2ReqSend
summary: Deci2Call(3, {s, (s8)cmd}) — cmd sign-extended from byte. Used by the TTY write path F_01023398.

name: sceDeci2Poll
summary: Deci2Call(4, {s}); used by TTY write to pump the connection.

name: sceDeci2ExRecv
summary: Deci2Call(-5, {s, buf, len&0xffff}); confirmed as receive by the TTY handler using it in the READ event with error string 'TTY: receive error' @0x1040778.
sig: int sceDeci2ExRecv(int s, void *buf, unsigned short len)

name: sceDeci2ExSend
summary: Deci2Call(-6, {s, buf, len&0xffff}); used by the TTY handler WRITE event, error 'TTY: send err %d' @0x1040790.
sig: int sceDeci2ExSend(int s, void *buf, unsigned short len)

name: sceDeci2ExReqSend
summary: MISSED-BY-DETECTOR function start (after F_01023078's padding): Deci2Call(-7, {s, (s8)cmd}) — sign-extends the byte exactly like sceDeci2ReqSend.

name: sceDeci2ExLock
summary: Deci2Call(-8, {s}).

name: sceDeci2ExUnLock
summary: Deci2Call(-9, {s}).

name: kPuts
summary: Deci2Call(0x10, {s}) — kernel puts to DECI2/EE kernel console. Called from F_0101C9C8 (libkernl Kprintf/internal-error printer).

name: tty_ring_init
summary: Initializes the TTY input ring @0x104d940: {+0 size, +4 count=0, +8 rp, +0xc wp, data from +0x10}; returns the ring pointer. Called from the TTY init F_010235B8.

name: tty_ring_put
summary: count++, advances write pointer with wrap at base+0x10+size (the caller stores the byte at *wp first).

name: tty_ring_get
summary: count--, advances read pointer with wrap; caller (F_010234E8, the read() backend) fetches *rp before calling.

name: deci2_tty_handler
summary: DECI2 TTY event callback (registered by F_010235B8 via sceDeci2Open): event 3 (WRITE) sends ctx->wbuf via sceDeci2ExSend ('TTY: send err %d'); event 4 (WRITEDONE) checks residual wlen ('TTY: err ti->wlen=%08x' @0x10407a8); events 1/2 (READ) pull data with sceDeci2ExRecv into ctx->rbuf (max 0x140, else 'TTY: packet size larger than expect' @0x1040750) and on len==0 parse the DECI2 packet (12-byte header, u16 total length) pushing payload bytes into the input ring. Errors printed via F_0101D270 (libkernl Kprintf).
sig: static void deci2_tty_handler(int event, int len, TtyCtx *ctx)

name: _deci2_tty_write
summary: Sends up to 256 bytes of console output to the host as one DECI2 TTYP packet: waits on busy flag at 0x104DA5C, copies bytes into the uncached packet buffer 0x2000_0000|0x104DA80 (payload at +0xC) converting LF(0x0A) to CR+LF, writes u16 packet length into the DECI2 header, then sceDeci2ReqSend(sd, dst='H' from header+7) via F_01022FE8 and polls with sceDeci2Poll (F_01023018) until the completion handler clears the flag. Returns source bytes consumed, or -1 if a send is already in flight. Behavior certain; exact Sony symbol unknown (kernel-TTY write used by libkernl printf via F_01022CF0).

name: _deci2_tty_read
summary: Blocking console read from host over DECI2 TTYP: for each byte spin-waits on the recv-ring 'data available' word (+4 of the ring object at *(0x104DA68)), copies one byte from the ring's read pointer (+8), advances the ring via F_010231C0, and stops after storing LF (0x0A) or CR (0x0D). Returns count read. Line-oriented gets() backend used by F_01022D70.

name: _deci2_tty_init
summary: Opens the DECI2 TTYP console: calls helper F_0101BE60(0), then sceDeci2Open(0x210, &state@0x104DA50, handler F_01023200) via F_01022F78; on success zeroes state fields, sets uncached send buffer 0x2000_0000|0x104DA80 (+0x10) and recv buffer |0x104DBC0 (+0x14), pre-fills the DECI2 header {u16 len, u16 0, u16 proto=0x210, u8 src='E', u8 dst='H', u32 0}, and allocates a 0x100-byte recv ring via F_01023158(0x100) stored at +0x18. Returns 1 on success, 0 if sceDeci2Open failed. Protocol 0x210 = DECI2 TTYP.

name: __divdi3
summary: libgcc signed 64-bit division (udivmoddi4 body inlined). Negates negative operands tracking result sign in $t7, normalizes divisor using count-leading-zero byte table at 0x10407C0 (private __clz_tab copy), performs 16-bit-digit schoolbook division with divu/mult3, negates quotient if signs differed. Sole caller: F_0101CCA8, libkernl printf's integer formatter.
sig: long long __divdi3(long long n, long long d)

name: __fixunsdfdi
summary: libgcc2 double -> u64 conversion: returns 0 if __cmpdf2(a,0)<0; hi = __fixunsdfsi(a * 2^-32) (constant 0x3DF0000000000000 built as 0xF7C0<<46), then adds/subtracts __fixunsdfsi of the residue a - __floatdidf(hi<<32). Caller F_0101CB40 (printf %f/%e formatter).

name: __floatdidf
summary: libgcc2 s64 -> double: __floatsidf(hi32), multiplied twice by 2^16 (constant 0x40F0000000000000 built as 0x81E0<<47), plus __floatsidf(lo32) corrected by +2^32 (0x41F0000000000000 = 0x83E0<<47) when the low word is negative. Called only by __fixunsdfdi.

name: __moddi3
summary: libgcc signed 64-bit modulo: same udivmoddi4 body with remainder pointer ($t9=$sp), private __clz_tab copy at 0x10408C0, remainder negated iff dividend was negative ($s0 flag), returns ld($sp). Sole caller F_0101CCA8 (printf integer formatter).
sig: long long __moddi3(long long n, long long d)

name: __udivdi3
summary: libgcc unsigned 64-bit division, no sign handling, no remainder pointer; private __clz_tab copy at 0x10409C0. Sole caller F_0101CCA8 (printf unsigned/hex 64-bit formatting).
sig: unsigned long long __udivdi3(unsigned long long n, unsigned long long d)

name: __umoddi3
summary: libgcc unsigned 64-bit modulo: udivmoddi4 body with remainder pointer $t8=$sp, private __clz_tab copy at 0x1040AC0, returns remainder from stack. Sole caller F_0101CCA8.
sig: unsigned long long __umoddi3(unsigned long long n, unsigned long long d)

name: pack_d
summary: fp-bit.c: packs {class,sign,normal_exp,fraction} into an IEEE-754 double bit pattern (returned in $v0). class<2 (NaN) -> exp 0x7FF with quiet bit 1<<59; class 4 (INF) -> exp 0x7FF frac 0; class 2 (ZERO) -> 0; NUMBER handles denormal shift, round-to-nearest-even on the low 8 guard bits, exponent bias +0x3FF; ORs sign<<63. Called by all pack sites incl. F_01025CA0/F_01025CD8 in the next chunk.

name: unpack_d
summary: fp-bit.c: loads the raw 64-bit double via ld($a0), splits sign (+4), exponent, 52-bit fraction; exp==0 -> class 2 ZERO (denormals flushed), exp==0x7FF -> INF(4) or QNAN(1)/SNAN(0) by bit 51, else class 3 NUMBER with fraction<<8 | implicit bit at bit 60 (+0x10) and unbiased exp (+8). 9 callers, incl. next-chunk fp-bit functions.

name: _fpadd_parts
summary: fp-bit.c addition core: NaN propagation, INF+(-INF) -> returns static NaN parts at 0x104DD00 (.bss), zero shortcuts, aligns exponents by shifting fractions with sticky bit (shifts >=0x40 zero the fraction), adds or subtracts fractions by sign, renormalizes (right shift on carry past bit 61, left-shift loop while below 1<<59). Called only by __adddf3 and __subdf3.

name: __adddf3
summary: fp-bit double add: unpack_d both operands into stack parts, _fpadd_parts, pack_d. Callers: __fixunsdfdi and __floatdidf.

name: __subdf3
summary: fp-bit double subtract: identical to __adddf3 but XORs b's sign field (+0x24 on stack) with 1 before _fpadd_parts. Callers: F_0101CB40 (printf float formatter) and __fixunsdfdi.

name: __muldf3
summary: fp-bit double multiply: unpacks both, NaN/INF/ZERO cases (INF*0 -> static NaN at 0x104DD00), sign=xor, then 64x64->128 fraction product via four 32x32->64 calls to helper F_01018070 (umul_ppmm), rounds with sticky/guard handling and renormalizes exponent (sum+4 adjust). Callers: F_0101CB40 (printf %f), __fixunsdfdi, __floatdidf.

name: __divdf3
summary: fp-bit double divide: unpacks both, sign=xor, NaN propagation, INF/INF and 0/0 -> static NaN 0x104DD00, x/INF -> 0, x/0 -> INF; otherwise bit-by-bit restoring division of fractions from mask 1<<61 with round-to-even at the end. Sole caller F_0101CB40 (printf float formatter).

name: __fpcmp_parts_d
summary: fp-bit compare on unpacked parts: any NaN -> 1; INF and ZERO ordering by sign; NUMBER compare by sign, then exponent, then 64-bit fraction; returns -1/0/1. Called only by __cmpdf2.

name: __cmpdf2
summary: fp-bit double compare: unpack_d both then __fpcmp_parts_d. Callers: F_0101CB40 (printf) and __fixunsdfdi (tests a<0.0).

name: __floatsidf
summary: fp-bit int -> double: 0 -> ZERO class; INT_MIN shortcut returns constant 0xC1E0000000000000 (-2^31); otherwise class NUMBER, sign=i>>31, exp=0x3C, |i| normalized left until bit 60, pack_d. Called only by __floatdidf.

name: __fixdfsi
summary: fp-bit double -> s32: NaN/ZERO -> 0, exp<0 -> 0, exp>=0x1F or INF -> saturate to 0x7FFFFFFF / 0x80000000 by sign, else fraction >> (0x3C-exp), negated if sign set. No callers in the callgraph - linked but dead.

name: __fixunsdfsi
summary: fp-bit double -> u32: NaN/ZERO -> 0, negative -> 0, INF or exp>=0x20 -> 0xFFFFFFFF, else fraction >> (0x3C-exp). Sole caller __fixunsdfdi.

name: __negdf2
summary: Double negate: unpacks via unpack_d (F_01025198, prev chunk), flips sign word with sltiu (sign = !sign), repacks via pack_d (F_01025068). Double arrives in $a0 as a 64-bit GPR (sd $a0), confirming soft-double ABI.

name: __make_dp
summary: fp-bit helper that builds an unpacked double struct {0:class,4:sign,8:exp,0x10:frac64 (sd $a3)} on the stack and tail-packs it with pack_d (F_01025068). Sole caller is __extendsfdf2 (F_01026900).
sig: double __make_dp(int cls, unsigned sign, int exp, unsigned long long frac)

name: __truncdfsf2
summary: Double-to-float: unpack_d, then narrows the 64-bit fraction to 32 bits ((frac<<2)>>32) with a sticky bit ORed in when the discarded low 30 bits (mask 0x3FFFFFFF) are nonzero, and calls __make_fp (F_010268D0).

name: pack_f
summary: fp-bit pack for single precision: rounds 7 guard bits (round-half-even test on 0x40/0x7F), handles NaN (exp=0xFF, frac|=0x00100000), zero and infinity, assembles (sign<<31)|(exp<<23)|frac23 and returns via mtc1 to $f0. Called by all sf entry points.

name: unpack_f
summary: fp-bit unpack for single precision: splits into class (0 SNAN/1 QNAN by bit 0x00100000, 2 ZERO for exp==0, 3 NUMBER, 4 INFINITY), sign, unbiased exp (e-0x7F), and fraction<<7 with implicit bit at 0x40000000 for normals.

name: _fpadd_parts
summary: fp-bit add core on unpacked floats: NaN propagation, inf-inf returns the static NaN object @0x104DD18 (.bss), aligns exponents with sticky right-shifts, adds/subtracts magnitudes (ldl/ldr/sdl/sdr struct copy for the trivial case), renormalizes with overflow shift.

name: __addsf3
summary: Single add: swc1 $f12/$f13 to stack, unpack_f both, _fpadd_parts, pack_f. No callers in the binary (dead code pulled in with fp-bit.o; EE has a hardware single FPU).

name: __subsf3
summary: Single subtract: identical to __addsf3 but XORs the second operand's sign field (xori 1 on sp+0x14) before _fpadd_parts.

name: __mulsf3
summary: Single multiply: full class dispatch (NaN propagation, 0*inf -> static NaN @0x104DD18, inf sign xor), multu of the two 31-bit fractions into a 64-bit product, exponent = ea+eb+2, right-normalizes negative-exp product with sticky bits, round-half-even fixup on 0x40/0x7F guard pattern.

name: __divsf3
summary: Single divide: 0/0 and inf/inf -> static NaN @0x104DD18, x/inf -> zero, x/0 -> inf; restoring shift-subtract division loop seeding quotient bit 0x40000000, exponent = ea-eb (adjusted), guard-bit round fixup, pack_f.

name: __fpcmp_parts_f
summary: Compare of two unpacked singles: any NaN -> 1; inf/zero/sign ordering; for numbers compares sign, then exp (slt), then fraction (sltu); returns -1/0/1.

name: __cmpsf2
summary: Thin wrapper: unpack_f both operands and return __fpcmp_parts_f. The only compare entry point emitted from fp-bit.o (could equally be the shared body behind __eq/__lt aliases, but __cmpsf2 is the gcc 2.9x fp-bit export). No callers — dead code.

name: __floatsisf
summary: int-to-float: 0 -> CLASS_ZERO; INT_MIN special-cased to the constant 0xCF000000 (-2^31f) via mtc1; otherwise class 3, sign=i>>31, exp=0x1E, frac=|i| normalized left until >=0x40000000, then pack_f.

name: __fixsfsi
summary: float-to-signed-int: NaN/zero -> 0; infinity or exp>=0x1F -> 0x7FFFFFFF / 0x80000000 by sign (movn); else frac >> (0x1E-exp), negated when sign set.

name: __fixunssfsi
summary: float-to-unsigned-int: NaN/zero/exp<0 -> 0; infinity or exp>=0x20 -> 0xFFFFFFFF; exp==0x1F..: frac << (exp-0x1E), else frac >> (0x1E-exp). Sign field never consulted (standard fp-bit behavior).

name: __negsf2
summary: Single negate: unpack_f, sign = (sign==0), pack_f. Mirror of __negdf2 at 0x01025CA0.

name: __make_fp
summary: fp-bit helper building an unpacked single {0:class,4:sign,8:exp,0xC:frac} on the stack and tail-packing via pack_f. Called by __truncdfsf2 (F_01025D08).
sig: float __make_fp(int cls, unsigned sign, int exp, unsigned frac)

name: __extendsfdf2
summary: float-to-double: unpack_f, widens fraction to 64 bits (dsll32 then dsrl 2 = frac<<30) and calls __make_dp. The only live-called sf routine: caller F_0101CCA8 (1.5KB, calls the __adddf3/__muldf3-family — almost certainly the printf %f/%g double-formatting core).

name: __errno
summary: Returns the errno cell: loads the _impure_ptr-style pointer @0x103DDD4 (-> struct _reent @0x103DAE8, _errno at offset 0). Callers F_01022DE8/F_01022F28/F_01022F50 store 5 (EIO) then return -1, and F_01022E28 (sbrk: break var @0x103DAE0, EndOfHeap check, di/ei critical section) stores 12 (ENOMEM). Newlib-derived Sony ee libc.

name: memcmp
summary: EE-optimized memcmp: when both pointers are 16-aligned and n>=16, compares quadwords with lq/lq + pxor + pcpyud/or (128-bit equality test), rewinding on mismatch; byte tail loop returns s1[i]-s2[i]. Callers F_0101F0F0 and F_01022020 (libpad/libmc region).
sig: int memcmp(const void *s1, const void *s2, size_t n)

name: sceGsGetGParam
summary: Named ELF section .text.sceGsGetGParam (per CONTEXT layout). Returns &GParam @0x01039500 — in libgraph .data immediately after the 'PsIIlibgraph2221' version tag @0x010394F0.

name: sceGsResetGraph
summary: Named ELF section .text.sceGsResetGraph. mode 0: writes GS CSR (0x12001000)=0x200 (RESET), sets GS IMR=0xFF00 via F_0101BF20 (GsPutIMR wrapper), fills GParam {im, omode, ffmd!=0, GS revision = CSR>>16 & 0xFF}, and if a vsync handler is installed (GParam+8) calls F_0101C2D0(2) and F_0101B8E0(2, GParam+0xC) (DisableIntc/RemoveIntcHandler on INTC 2 = VBLANK_START) then clears both; tail-jumps F_0101B7E0 = SetGsCrt(im&1, omode&0xFF, ffmd&1) syscall wrapper. mode 1: CSR=0x100 (FLUSH) only. mode 5: refills GParam + SetGsCrt without reset or handler removal.
sig: int sceGsResetGraph(short mode, short im, short omode, short ffmd)
